title: Coughing habits and breath hygiene in shared areas
audience: Cleaning and service workers in hospitals, clinics, aged care and dental sites who move through waiting rooms, corridors and lifts.
learningOutcomes: Describe how respiratory droplets reach surfaces and other people in a shared area.
Apply the coughing habit and the hand cleaning step that follows it.
Report a respiratory symptom or an empty supply to a supervisor without confronting the person.

instruction.heading: Why breath and cough matter in a service area
instruction.body: Some germs leave the body in the small drops produced when someone coughs, sneezes or speaks, and a few remain in the air for longer. A worker who walks through a waiting room, a corridor or a lift can collect these on the hands, then carry them to the lips, the nostrils or the eyes. Respiratory hygiene is the group of habits that stops those drops reaching the next person or the next object. The guideline starts these habits at the moment of first contact, which for a cleaner usually means meeting a visitor or patient in a shared space.

instruction.heading: What you do about your own cough
instruction.body: When you cough or sneeze yourself, hold a tissue over your nose and mouth. Without a tissue, turn your face into the crook of the arm rather than using a palm, since hands spread germs onto everything they reach. Drop the used tissue into the closest lidded bin, then clean your hands. Hand cleaning applies again after any touch of an object that has been near someone's breath or secretions, such as a tissue resting on a chair.

instruction.heading: Supporting the system around you
instruction.body: The facility should stock tissues, lidded bins and hand cleaning products at the points where people need them. Your task is to spot an empty dispenser or an overflowing bin and report it. Never confront someone who is coughing. Pass the concern to your supervisor, who can apply the site policy. That policy may ask a symptomatic person to wear a mask and to keep a gap from other people in shared spaces. The source sets a specific gap distance.

procedure: Notice a coughing visitor or patient in a shared area, and keep your distance without staring.
Keep your fingers away from your face, eyes and mouth while you work there.
Clean your hands after touching a used tissue or any surface a coughing person has handled.
Report an empty tissue dispenser or an overflowing bin to your supervisor in the same shift.
If someone with symptoms is inside a care area, inform your supervisor and let site policy decide the response.
Log the report in your shift record, with the time and place.

workedExamples.situation: While mopping a waiting room, a cleaner sees a visitor cough into an open palm and then press the lift call button.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What should the cleaner do next?
workedExamples.reasoning: Clean their own hands at the closest basin or dispenser. Pass the touch point and the time to the supervisor, so the site can arrange a wipe and apply its response. The cleaner does not argue with the visitor.

workedExamples.situation: A used tissue sits on a seat in the waiting area, and the nearest bin is two metres away.
workedExamples.reasoning: Lift the tissue with gloves if the site requires them, put it in the bin, then clean your hands. Check the seat against the cleaning schedule. Leaving the tissue where it lies does not meet the standard.

equipmentAndPpe: Disposable gloves for lifting used tissues or soiled items
Hand cleaning product at the basin or wall dispenser
Tissues and lidded bins supplied by the facility

commonErrors.error: Coughing into the palm, then handling door handles or lift buttons.
commonErrors.prevention: Use the elbow when no tissue is available, and clean your hands before the next touch.

commonErrors.error: Regarding a visitor's cough as someone else's problem.
commonErrors.prevention: Report what you saw to the supervisor, so that site policy can be applied.

commonErrors.error: Leaving used tissues on the ground, or in an open bag.
commonErrors.prevention: Put the tissue into the nearest lidded bin, then clean your hands.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Cover every cough and sneeze straight away, because hands carry germs from the face to other surfaces.
This lesson does not decide whether someone is infectious or needs a mask. Those decisions belong to the clinical team and site policy.
Site policy and the NHMRC guideline govern.

qualityStandard: Hands are cleaned after each contact with a used tissue or a surface touched by a coughing person.
Each report names the location, the time and the item affected.
documentationEvidence: Shift record entry for any empty dispenser, overflowing bin or respiratory-symptom report
Name of the supervisor who took the report
summary: Use a tissue, or the crook of the arm, for a cough; bin the tissue; clean your hands.
Report symptoms and empty supplies, and never confront a person.

knowledgeChecks.question: A visitor coughs into an open hand and then presses the lift button in front of you. What is the best response?
options: Continue, because visitors are not your responsibility and the touch point will be cleaned by the visitor later
Clean your hands, then tell the supervisor which touch point was affected so that site policy can be applied.
Wipe the button with your bare hand, then keep working and then wipe your hand on your uniform
Confront the visitor and tell them to leave the building and ask them to sign the visitor book

knowledgeChecks.question: Which action best follows cough etiquette in a work area?
options: Hold a tissue over your nose and mouth, or use the crook of your arm if no tissue is available.
Cough into your palm and then wipe your hands on your uniform and then carry on with the work
Hold your breath and cough into a sleeve you have just used and wipe the sleeve on the bench
Turn away from people, cough, and continue working and wipe the table with your hand

knowledgeChecks.question: After you handle a used tissue from a bin, what comes next?
options: Hand cleaning, because the tissue may have carried respiratory secretions.
Nothing, because the tissue went into a bin and the bin lid was closed
Changing into a new uniform only and then go back to the ward at once
Emptying the bin into a second bag before washing the bin lid.
